name: Make an ad test set from one product brief: 5 angles and headlines in every ad size, saved to Drive and a sheet (MartLLM)

parameters.content:
## An ad test set from one product brief

Fill in a short form: a product photo, the product name, and who it is for. A text model writes 5 different angles, each with a headline and a primary text. An image model then makes each angle as an ad image in every size you chose (square, portrait and vertical by default), from your real photo so the product stays the same. Every image is saved to a new Google Drive folder and listed in a Google Sheet with its headline, size and cost, ready to load into your ad account.

Nothing is posted or launched anywhere.

### Set up (10 minutes)
1. Get an API key at [martllm.com](https://martllm.com/go/n8n-ad-creative-test-set) and add credit.
2. Open **Save the photo** → Credential → Create new → **Header Auth**:
   - Name: `Authorization`
   - Value: `Bearer ` followed by your key
   The other MartLLM steps use the same credential. If you already made it for another MartLLM or UberLLM template, pick that one.
3. Open **Make a Drive folder** and **Save to the Drive folder** and connect Google Drive.
4. Open **Add the row to the sheet**: connect Google Sheets and pick a spreadsheet and tab. An empty tab is fine: the column names are written on the first run.
5. Activate the workflow, open **Brief form** and copy its link.

### Price
Listed on 2026-11-25: $0.0079 per image (Nano Banana), so 5 angles in 3 sizes = 15 images, about $0.12. The ad copy costs a fraction of a cent. The workflow reads the real price of every image before it makes the first one. Prices move: [live prices](https://martllm.com/models).

### What you pay
- Each request costs what the seller that made it charged. No MartLLM fee on requests.
- Anything that is not made costs nothing.
- Adding credit by card costs 5.5% + $0.50. Credit does not expire while your account is open.

### Change it here
**Settings** holds the number of angles, the sizes (`1:1` square, `4:5` portrait feed, `9:16` stories and reels, `16:9` wide), the models, the most one run may cost and the rules for the ad copy.

Any image-edit model on [martllm.com/models](https://martllm.com/models) works: copy its id.

### Price first
The price of every image is read before the first one is made. Nothing is charged for that. If the set would cost more than `max_total_cost_usd`, or a size is one the model does not make, the form stops here with the reason.

### One ad at a time
An image that cannot be made does not stop the others. Its row in the sheet says why, in the API's own words, and it costs nothing. MartLLM keeps an image link for about 15 minutes, so each image is saved to Drive at once.

### Before you run these
Look at every image: a model can change a label or a colour. People in the images are AI-generated; label them where your ad platform asks for it, and never present one as a real customer.

parameters.formDescription: Upload one clear photo of your product and tell us who it is for. You get 5 ad angles, each with a headline, as images in every ad size. It takes a few minutes; keep this page open.

values.fieldLabel: Who is it for, and why do they buy it?
values.placeholder: e.g. Commuters who walk a lot. Light, breathable, machine washable. Honest and casual tone.

assignments.name: copy_instructions
assignments.value:
You plan ad creative tests for online stores. You get a product name, who it is for and why they buy it, and how many angles to write.

Write that many angles that are clearly different from each other, so a test can tell which idea works: for example the main benefit, a problem it solves, a moment of use, who it is for, what makes it different. Use only what the brief says. Never invent prices, discounts, reviews, numbers, awards or health claims.

For each angle write:
- angle: two to four words that name the idea
- headline: at most 40 characters
- primary_text: one or two sentences, at most 125 characters
- image_prompt: one sentence that describes a photo for this angle: where the product is, what surrounds it, the light and the mood. The product itself comes from a real photo, so do not describe the product. No text in the image.

Answer with JSON only: {"variants": [{"angle": "...", "headline": "...", "primary_text": "...", "image_prompt": "..."}]}
